subproblems.title: Two unit orientations of the same n-plane differ by a sign
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P and let v, w ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n: continuous linear functionals on n-covectors, ⟨α, v⟩ = v(α)). If v and w are both unit orientations of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf v Q and IsUnitOrientationOf w Q: for some orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P spanning Q, v(α) = ±α(τ) and w(α) = ±α(τ') for all n-covectors α), then w = v or w = −v.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v w : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf v Q → IsUnitOrientationOf w Q → w = v ∨ w = -v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem (the sign lemma: two orthonormal frames τ, τ' of the same n-plane differ by a change of frame B with det B = ±1, so α(τ') = det(B)·α(τ) for every n-covector α), which justifies "ξ_T(x) = ±ξ_S(x)" there. This is the linear algebra behind Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756, stated without proof; an orientation ξ = τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ pairs with an n-covector α as α(τ₁, …, τₙ), Simon 6.1 and 3.1). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.integer_combination-a1.orientation_sign-a1, status accepted, candidate fe95347), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. The title, statement and Lean type are copied from its DAG record, and the numbered argument below is copied verbatim from its accepted handoff; the accepted formalization follows it.

1. Unfolding the hypotheses: there are orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q = span(range τ'), and signs ε, ε' ∈ {1, −1} with v(α) = ε·α(τ) and w(α) = ε'·α(τ') for every n-covector α (continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ).

2. Each τ_i and τ'_i lies in Q, so τ, τ' may be regarded as families in the inner product space Q, where they are still orthonormal. Since τ is linearly independent and spans Q, dim Q = n; an orthonormal (hence linearly independent) family of n vectors in the n-dimensional space Q spans Q. Hence τ and τ' are orthonormal bases b and b' of Q indexed by Fin n.

3. Let d := det_b(b'), the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix from b to b'. Both bases are orthonormal, so this matrix is orthogonal and d ∈ {1, −1} (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real).

4. Let α be an n-covector and α_Q its restriction to Q (α composed with the inclusion Q → ℝ^P in each slot), an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q. Every such form is a multiple of det_b: α_Q = α_Q(b)·det_b (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α(τ') = α_Q(b') = α_Q(b)·det_b(b') = d·α(τ). The number d does not depend on α.

5. Hence for every α: w(α) = ε'·α(τ') = ε'd·α(τ) = (εε'd)·(ε·α(τ)) = s·v(α), where s := εε'd ∈ {1, −1} (using ε² = 1). Therefore w = s·v, i.e. w = v if s = 1 and w = −v if s = −1. For n = 0 the same argument applies (τ = τ' is the empty family, Q = {0}, d = 1). ∎

Formalization (as in the accepted declaration, which compiles with axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound): the families are restricted to Q via Submodule.subset_span, made into OrthonormalBasis values by OrthonormalBasis.mk (spanning via Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun); step 3 is OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real (Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/PiL2.lean); step 4 is AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Determinant.lean) applied to α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap Q.subtype and evaluated at b'; step 5 is a case split over the three signs closed by ContinuousLinearMap extensionality.
proof_key_steps: Both orthonormal families spanning Q are orthonormal bases b, b' of Q.
det_b(b') = ±1 because the change-of-basis matrix is orthogonal.
For every n-covector α, α(τ') = det_b(b')·α(τ) since alternating n-forms on Q are multiples of det_b.
Therefore w = (εε'det_b(b'))·v with εε'det_b(b') ∈ {±1}.

subproblems.title: Orientations of two integer multiplicity triples agree up to sign on the overlap
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P, and let R₁ = (C₁, θ₁, ξ₁) and R₂ = (C₂, θ₂, ξ₂) be integer multiplicity triples in U (IMRep U n, Simon Ch. 6, 3.1). Write Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Assume that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂, every approximate tangent space of C₁ at x is an approximate tangent space of C₁ ∩ C₂ at x, i.e. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C₁ x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (C₁ ∩ C₂) x Q for every subspace Q. Assume also that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂, every approximate tangent space of C₂ at x is an approximate tangent space of C₁ ∩ C₂ at x, i.e. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C₂ x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (C₁ ∩ C₂) x Q for every subspace Q. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂, ξ₂(x) = ξ₁(x) or ξ₂(x) = −ξ₁(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R₁ R₂ : IMRep U n), (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R₁.carrier ∩ R₂.carrier)), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n R₁.carrier x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (R₁.carrier ∩ R₂.carrier) x Q) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R₁.carrier ∩ R₂.carrier)), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n R₂.carrier x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (R₁.carrier ∩ R₂.carrier) x Q) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R₁.carrier ∩ R₂.carrier)), R₂.orient x = R₁.orient x ∨ R₂.orient x = -R₁.orient x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem. Step 2 reads "for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C_S ∩ C_T the approximate tangent space Q_x of C at x exists and ξ_S(x), ξ_T(x) are both unit orientations of Q_x"; step 3 concludes "ξ_T(x) = ±ξ_S(x)". The locality input of step 2 is supplied here as the two explicit tangent-inheritance hypotheses; the selected theorem discharges them with its declared, accepted dependency approx_tangent_locality (Submission.regcomp_approx_tangent_locality) applied to C₁ ∩ C₂ ⊆ C₁ and to C₁ ∩ C₂ ⊆ C₂. Uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces is Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1) (chapter-03.txt line 86; SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Context: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756).

Notation: μ := μHE[n]; C_i := R_i.carrier and ξ_i := R_i.orient for i = 1, 2; I := C₁ ∩ C₂. The hypotheses are (H₁): for μ⌞I-a.e. x, every subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C₁ x Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n I x Q; and (H₂): the same with C₂ in place of C₁.

1. (Restricting the orientation conditions.) The field R₁.orients says that for μ⌞C₁-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C₁ x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ₁ x) Q. Since I ⊆ C₁, every μ⌞C₁-null set is μ⌞I-null, so the same holds for μ⌞I-a.e. x (Mathlib ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). Likewise R₂.orients holds μ⌞I-a.e., because I ⊆ C₂.

2. (A generic point.) The four statements — step 1 for R₁, step 1 for R₂, (H₁) and (H₂) — each hold for μ⌞I-a.e. x, hence they hold simultaneously for μ⌞I-a.e. x. Fix such an x. Step 1 provides subspaces Q₁, Q₂ with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C₁ x Q₁, IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ₁ x) Q₁, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C₂ x Q₂ and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ₂ x) Q₂.

3. (Common plane.) (H₁) applied to Q₁ gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n I x Q₁, and (H₂) applied to Q₂ gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n I x Q₂. The approximate tangent space of the set I at x is unique (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so Q₁ = Q₂.

4. (Sign.) Hence ξ₁ x and ξ₂ x are both unit orientations of the subspace Q₁. The sibling orientation_sign (Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg, applied with v := ξ₁ x, w := ξ₂ x, Q := Q₁) gives ξ₂ x = ξ₁ x ∨ ξ₂ x = −ξ₁ x. Since x was a μ⌞I-generic point, ξ₂ = ±ξ₁ holds μ⌞(C₁ ∩ C₂)-a.e., which is the claim. ∎

Formalization notes (checked by a complete scratch formalization in which the sibling is the only assumption; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound):
- Restrict with explicit ascriptions, which Lean needs to infer the smaller set: ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset (inter_subset_left : R₁.carrier ∩ R₂.carrier ⊆ R₁.carrier) R₁.orients, and the same with (inter_subset_right : R₁.carrier ∩ R₂.carrier ⊆ R₂.carrier) and R₂.orients.

subproblems.title: Carrier, multiplicity and orientation of the difference of two integer multiplicity triples
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R₁ R₂ : IMRep U n), (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R₁.carrier ∩ R₂.carrier)), R₂.orient x = R₁.orient x ∨ R₂.orient x = -R₁.orient x) → ∃ (C : Set (Euclid P)) (θ : Euclid P → ℕ) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), MeasurableSet C ∧ C ⊆ R₁.carrier ∪ R₂.carrier ∧ Measurable θ ∧ (∀ x ∈ C, 0 < θ x) ∧ (∀ x ∈ C, θ x ≤ R₁.carrier.indicator R₁.mult x + R₂.carrier.indicator R₂.mult x) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable ξ (μHE[n].restrict C) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (C ∩ R₁.carrier)), ξ x = R₁.orient x ∨ ξ x = -R₁.orient x) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (C \ R₁.carrier)), ξ x = R₂.orient x ∨ ξ x = -R₂.orient x) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], C.indicator (fun y => (θ y : ℝ) • ξ y) x = R₁.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₁.mult y : ℝ) • R₁.orient y) x - R₂.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₂.mult y : ℝ) • R₂.orient y) x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem ("Measurable bookkeeping": the Borel sign σ, d = θ_S − σθ_T, C', θ', ξ'), together with the pointwise computation of step 6 ("on C_S ∩ C_T the combined integrand is a.e. θ_S ξ_S(ω) − θ_T σ ξ_S(ω) = d ξ_S(ω) = |d| sign(d) ξ_S(ω), which vanishes where d = 0"), stated here at the level of n-vector densities. The multiplicity bound θ' ≤ θ_S + θ_T and the orientation signs used in step 5 are included. Context: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756).

Notation: μ := μHE[n]; C_i := R_i.carrier, θ_i := R_i.mult and ξ_i := R_i.orient for i = 1, 2. 1_S φ denotes the indicator (Set.indicator) of φ on S. Casts ℕ → ℤ → ℝ are left implicit.

1. (Borel versions.) By R_i.aestronglyMeasurable_orient, ξ_i is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞C_i. Let η_i := (R_i.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).mk ξ_i; it is strongly measurable, and ξ_i = η_i μ⌞C_i-a.e. Since C_i is measurable (R_i.measurableSet_carrier), ae_restrict_iff' turns this into
   (A_i) for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ C_i → ξ_i(x) = η_i(x).
   In the same way (C₁ ∩ C₂ is measurable) the hypothesis becomes
   (H) for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ C₁ → x ∈ C₂ → ξ₂(x) = ξ₁(x) ∨ ξ₂(x) = −ξ₁(x).

2. (Sign.) Let E := {x : η₂(x) = η₁(x)}. It is measurable because η₁, η₂ are strongly measurable with values in a metrizable space (StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun; see the notes for the instance). Put σ(x) := 1 if x ∈ E and σ(x) := −1 otherwise; σ : ℝ^P → ℤ is measurable.
   Claim (S): for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ C₁ → x ∈ C₂ → ξ₂(x) = σ(x)·ξ₁(x).
   Take x outside the null sets of (A₁), (A₂), (H), with x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂.
   - If x ∈ E: ξ₂(x) = η₂(x) = η₁(x) = ξ₁(x) = σ(x)ξ₁(x).
   - If x ∉ E: the alternative ξ₂(x) = ξ₁(x) of (H) is impossible, since it would give η₂(x) = ξ₂(x) = ξ₁(x) = η₁(x). Hence ξ₂(x) = −ξ₁(x) = σ(x)ξ₁(x).

3. (Multiplicity difference.) Let d(x) := θ₁(x) − σ(x)θ₂(x) ∈ ℤ. It is measurable: θ_i is measurable, and sums and products of measurable ℤ-valued functions are measurable. Let D := C₁ ∩ C₂ ∩ {x : d(x) ≠ 0}; it is measurable.

4. (Definitions.)
   C := (C₁ ∖ C₂) ∪ (C₂ ∖ C₁) ∪ D.
   θ(x) := |d(x)| (Int.natAbs) if x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂; θ₁(x) if x ∈ C₁ ∖ C₂; θ₂(x) if x ∈ C₂ ∖ C₁; 0 if x ∉ C₁ ∪ C₂.
   ξ(x) := sign(d(x))·η₁(x) if x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂; η₁(x) if x ∈ C₁ ∖ C₂; −η₂(x) if x ∉ C₁. Here sign = Int.sign, cast to ℝ.
   Thus x ∈ C iff (x ∈ C₁ ∧ x ∉ C₂) ∨ (x ∈ C₂ ∧ x ∉ C₁) ∨ (x ∈ C₁ ∧ x ∈ C₂ ∧ d(x) ≠ 0). The supplied proof defines ξ' with ξ_S, ξ_T. Using the Borel versions η_i changes ξ only on a μ⌞C-null set and makes measurability immediate.

5. (Measurability.)
   - C is a finite Boolean combination of the measurable sets C₁, C₂ and D.
   - θ is defined by cases on the measurable sets C₁, C₂ from the measurable functions |d| = Int.natAbs ∘ d, θ₁, θ₂ and 0 (Measurable.ite).
   - ξ is defined by cases on C₁, C₂ from three strongly measurable maps: x ↦ (sign(d(x)) : ℝ)·η₁(x) (a measurable real scalar function times a strongly measurable map), η₁ and −η₂ (StronglyMeasurable.ite, .smul, .neg). So ξ is strongly measurable, in particular a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞C.

6. (Carrier, positivity, bound.) Every piece of C lies in C₁ ∪ C₂, so C ⊆ C₁ ∪ C₂. Write b(x) := 1_{C₁}θ₁(x) + 1_{C₂}θ₂(x) ∈ ℕ. For x ∈ C:
   - x ∈ C₁ ∖ C₂: θ(x) = θ₁(x) > 0 (R₁.mult_pos), and b(x) = θ₁(x).
   - x ∈ C₂ ∖ C₁: θ(x) = θ₂(x) > 0 (R₂.mult_pos), and b(x) = θ₂(x).
   - x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂: then x ∈ D, so d(x) ≠ 0 and θ(x) = |d(x)| > 0. Moreover |d(x)| = |θ₁(x) − σ(x)θ₂(x)| ≤ θ₁(x) + θ₂(x) = b(x), because σ(x) = ±1 and θ_i(x) ≥ 0.

7. (Orientation signs on the pieces.) C ∩ C₁ and C ∖ C₁ are measurable, so ae_restrict_iff' reduces each claim to a μ-a.e. implication.
   (a) On C ∩ C₁: take x outside the null set of (A₁), with x ∈ C ∩ C₁.
       - If x ∉ C₂, then ξ(x) = η₁(x) = ξ₁(x).
       - If x ∈ C₂, then x ∈ D, so d(x) ≠ 0 and sign(d(x)) ∈ {1, −1} (Int.sign_eq_one_of_pos, Int.sign_eq_neg_one_of_neg). Hence ξ(x) = ±η₁(x) = ±ξ₁(x).
   (b) On C ∖ C₁: take x outside the null set of (A₂), with x ∈ C ∖ C₁. The only piece of C outside C₁ is C₂ ∖ C₁, so x ∈ C₂, and ξ(x) = −η₂(x) = −ξ₂(x).

8. (Density identity.) Let x lie outside the μ-null exceptional sets of (A₁), (A₂) and (S). Compare lhs(x) := 1_C(x)θ(x)ξ(x) with rhs(x) := 1_{C₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) − 1_{C₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ₂(x).
   - x ∉ C₁ ∪ C₂: x ∉ C, so lhs(x) = 0 = 0 − 0 = rhs(x).
   - x ∈ C₁ ∖ C₂: x ∈ C, and lhs(x) = θ₁(x)η₁(x) = θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) = rhs(x).
   - x ∈ C₂ ∖ C₁: x ∈ C, and lhs(x) = θ₂(x)·(−η₂(x)) = −θ₂(x)ξ₂(x) = rhs(x).
   - x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂: by (S), rhs(x) = θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) − θ₂(x)σ(x)ξ₁(x) = d(x)ξ₁(x).
     · If d(x) ≠ 0: x ∈ D ⊆ C, and lhs(x) = |d(x)|·sign(d(x))·η₁(x) = d(x)ξ₁(x). This uses |a|·sign(a) = a for a ∈ ℤ (Int.sign_mul_natAbs, cast to ℝ) and η₁(x) = ξ₁(x).
     · If d(x) = 0: x lies in neither difference and not in D, so x ∉ C and lhs(x) = 0 = 0·ξ₁(x) = rhs(x).
   Hence lhs = rhs μ-a.e. Together with steps 4–7, (C, θ, ξ) has every required property. ∎

Formalization notes (checked by a complete scratch formalization; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound):
- Borel versions: ⟨_, R₁.aestronglyMeasurable_orient.stronglyMeasurable_mk, (ae_restrict_iff' hC₁).mp R₁.aestronglyMeasurable_orient.ae_eq_mk⟩ gives η₁ with ∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], x ∈ R₁.carrier → R₁.orient x = η₁ x; similarly for η₂.
- Instance search does not find TopologicalSpace.MetrizableSpace (MultiVector P n) with the ContinuousLinearMap topology. Inside the proof use have : TopologicalSpace.MetrizableSpace (MultiVector P n) := { toPseudoMetrizableSpace := ⟨⟨PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace, rfl, Metric.uniformity_basis_dist_inv_nat_succ.isCountablyGenerated⟩⟩, toT0Space := inferInstance }, then hη₂.measurableSet_eq_fun hη₁.
- For StronglyMeasurable.neg, supply have : ContinuousNeg (MultiVector P n) := @IsTopologicalAddGroup.toContinuousNeg _ _ _ ContinuousLinearMap.isTopologicalAddGroup.
- Measurability:
  · σ: Measurable.ite hE measurable_const measurable_const.
  · d: (measurable_from_nat.comp R₁.measurable_mult).sub (hσm.mul (measurable_from_nat.comp R₂.measurable_mult)).
  · θ: nested Measurable.ite with (measurable_of_countable Int.natAbs).comp hdm.
  · The sign factor: ((measurable_of_countable fun k : ℤ => (k.sign : ℝ)).comp hdm).stronglyMeasurable.
- Generic module rewrites (sub_zero, zero_sub, neg_smul, one_smul) may fail to fire on MultiVector P n. Prove each n-vector identity pointwise: ext α; simp. Or use simp only [sub_apply, smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] followed by ring or linear_combination.
- The bound |d| ≤ θ₁ + θ₂: unfold σ and d, then split_ifs <;> omega.
- Write Set.mem_sdiff qualified (the bare name is ambiguous with Filter.mem_sdiff). Prefer ite_true/ite_false to the deprecated if_true/if_false.
proof_key_steps: Take Borel versions η_i of the orientations. The measurable sign σ = ±1, according to whether η₂ = η₁, satisfies ξ₂ = σξ₁ a.e. on C₁ ∩ C₂.
Set d = θ₁ − σθ₂ ∈ ℤ, C = (C₁∖C₂) ∪ (C₂∖C₁) ∪ {x ∈ C₁ ∩ C₂ : d ≠ 0}, θ = θ₁, θ₂, |d| and ξ = η₁, −η₂, sign(d)η₁ on the respective pieces.
Measurability, positivity and the bound θ ≤ 1_{C₁}θ₁ + 1_{C₂}θ₂ on C, using |θ₁ − σθ₂| ≤ θ₁ + θ₂.
Orientation signs: ξ = ±ξ₁ a.e. on C ∩ C₁ and ξ = −ξ₂ a.e. on C ∖ C₁.
A case analysis (outside C₁ ∪ C₂; C₁∖C₂; C₂∖C₁; the overlap with d ≠ 0 or d = 0) gives 1_Cθξ = 1_{C₁}θ₁ξ₁ − 1_{C₂}θ₂ξ₂ a.e.

subproblems.title: A triple glued with signs from two integer multiplicity triples is an integer multiplicity triple
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U C : Set (Euclid P)) (R₁ R₂ : IMRep U n) (θ : Euclid P → ℕ) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), MeasurableSet C → C ⊆ R₁.carrier ∪ R₂.carrier → Measurable θ → (∀ x ∈ C, 0 < θ x) → (∀ x ∈ C, θ x ≤ R₁.carrier.indicator R₁.mult x + R₂.carrier.indicator R₂.mult x) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ (μHE[n].restrict C) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (C ∩ R₁.carrier)), ξ x = R₁.orient x ∨ ξ x = -R₁.orient x) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (C \ R₁.carrier)), ξ x = R₂.orient x ∨ ξ x = -R₂.orient x) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (C ∩ R₁.carrier)), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n R₁.carrier x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (C \ R₁.carrier)), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n R₂.carrier x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q) → ∃ R : IMRep U n, R.carrier = C ∧ R.mult = θ ∧ R.orient = ξ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem ("R' := (C', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in U"). Its locality input is supplied here as the two tangent-inheritance hypotheses; the selected theorem discharges them with its declared, accepted dependency approx_tangent_locality (Submission.regcomp_approx_tangent_locality). The two pieces are C ∩ C₁ (the supplied proof's P₁ ∪ P₃) and C ∖ C₁ (its P₂ ⊆ C₂). The definition being verified is Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–745), as frozen in the contract's IMRep.

Notation: μ := μHE[n]; C_i := R_i.carrier, θ_i := R_i.mult and ξ_i := R_i.orient. We verify the fields of IMRep U n for (C, θ, ξ).

1. measurableSet_carrier: MeasurableSet C is a hypothesis.

2. carrier_subset: C ⊆ C₁ ∪ C₂ ⊆ U, by hypothesis and R₁.carrier_subset, R₂.carrier_subset.

3. rectifiable: Let M : ℕ → Set (Euclid P) be M 0 := C₁ and M (i+1) := C₂. Each M i is countably n-rectifiable (R₁.rectifiable, R₂.rectifiable), so ⋃ i, M i is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion). Since C ⊆ C₁ ∪ C₂ ⊆ ⋃ i, M i, C is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono).

4. measurable_mult and mult_pos: hypotheses.

5. locallyIntegrable_mult. Let K ⊆ U be compact, and write g_i := 1_{C_i}·(θ_i : ℝ≥0∞), a measurable function.
   - For x ∈ C ∩ K, (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ g₁(x) + g₂(x). This is the hypothesis θ(x) ≤ 1_{C₁}θ₁(x) + 1_{C₂}θ₂(x) cast to ℝ≥0∞, by a case split on x ∈ C₁ and x ∈ C₂.
   - Then:
     ∫⁻_{C∩K} θ dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{C∩K} (g₁ + g₂) dμ  [setLIntegral_mono', C ∩ K measurable]
       ≤ ∫⁻_K (g₁ + g₂) dμ  [lintegral_mono_set, since C ∩ K ⊆ K]
       = ∫⁻_K g₁ dμ + ∫⁻_K g₂ dμ  [lintegral_add_left, g₁ measurable]
       = ∫⁻_{C₁∩K} θ₁ dμ + ∫⁻_{C₂∩K} θ₂ dμ  [lintegral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict].
   - Both summands are ≠ ∞ by R₁.locallyIntegrable_mult K and R₂.locallyIntegrable_mult K. Hence ∫⁻_{C∩K} θ dμ ≠ ∞.

6. aestronglyMeasurable_orient: hypothesis.

7. orients.
   (a) Negation. Suppose IsUnitOrientationOf v Q via τ, i.e. v(α) = α(τ) for all α or v(α) = −α(τ) for all α. Then IsUnitOrientationOf (−v) Q via the same τ, with the other alternative, since (−v)(α) = −v(α). Hence w = v ∨ w = −v together with IsUnitOrientationOf v Q gives IsUnitOrientationOf w Q.
   (b) Piece C ∩ C₁. R₁.orients holds μ⌞C₁-a.e., hence μ⌞(C ∩ C₁)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset, C ∩ C₁ ⊆ C₁). Intersect with the sign hypothesis and the inheritance hypothesis on C ∩ C₁. At such x:
       - R₁.orients gives Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C₁ x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ₁ x) Q;
       - inheritance gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q;
       - (a) gives IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q.
   (c) Piece C ∖ C₁. Since C ⊆ C₁ ∪ C₂, C ∖ C₁ ⊆ C₂. So R₂.orients holds μ⌞(C ∖ C₁)-a.e., and the same argument with the C ∖ C₁ hypotheses gives the conclusion there.
   (d) Union. (C ∩ C₁) ∪ (C ∖ C₁) = C (Set.inter_union_sdiff). By ae_restrict_union_iff, "∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q" therefore holds μ⌞C-a.e.

8. (Conclusion.) R := IMRep.mk C θ ξ, with the proofs of steps 1–7. Its carrier, multiplicity and orientation are C, θ and ξ by rfl. ∎

Formalization notes (checked by a complete scratch formalization; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound):
- The contract header does not open countablyRectifiable_iUnion. Use Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_iUnion (fun i : ℕ => if i = 0 then R₁.carrier else R₂.carrier) (with split_ifs for the pieces), then .mono.
- In step 5, the cast step is simp only [Set.indicator] at h ⊢; split_ifs at h ⊢ <;> exact_mod_cast h. The chain closes with rw [lintegral_add_left (hθ₁e.indicator hC₁), lintegral_indicator hC₁, lintegral_indicator hC₂, Measure.restrict_restrict hC₁, Measure.restrict_restrict hC₂] inside ne_top_of_le_ne_top with ENNReal.add_ne_top.
- In 7(b), write ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset (inter_subset_right : C ∩ R₁.carrier ⊆ R₁.carrier) R₁.orients; the type ascription is needed.
- In 7(d), use have h := (ae_restrict_union_iff (C ∩ R₁.carrier) (C \ R₁.carrier) _).mpr ⟨h₁, h₂⟩; rwa [Set.inter_union_sdiff] at h. This rewrites only the measure. Never rewrite C itself, because C also occurs inside HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q.
- Conclude with ⟨IMRep.mk C θ ξ hC (hCsub.trans (union_subset R₁.carrier_subset R₂.carrier_subset)) hrect hθ hθpos hlocint hξ horient, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩.
proof_key_steps: Carrier fields: C is Borel, C ⊆ C₁ ∪ C₂ ⊆ U, and C is countably n-rectifiable as a subset of C₁ ∪ C₂.
Local integrability: ∫_{C∩K} θ ≤ ∫_{C₁∩K} θ₁ + ∫_{C₂∩K} θ₂ < ∞, using θ ≤ 1_{C₁}θ₁ + 1_{C₂}θ₂.
Orientation on C ∩ C₁ (resp. C ∖ C₁ ⊆ C₂): R₁.orients (resp. R₂.orients) together with tangent inheritance and closure of unit orientations under negation.
Combine the two pieces via ae_restrict_union_iff and assemble IMRep.mk C θ ξ.

subproblems.title: An a.e. identity of weighted orientations yields the integer combination of the represented currents
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁), R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂), R = (M, θ, ξ) be IMReps in U (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1) and p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ. Suppose that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) the n-vectors satisfy 1_M(x)θ(x)ξ(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ₂(x). Then for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (ω : TestFormOn U n) we have τ(R)(ω) = p₁τ(R₁)(ω) + p₂τ(R₂)(ω), where τ(R)(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R₁ R₂ R : IMRep U n) (p₁ p₂ : ℤ), (∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], R.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R.mult y : ℝ) • R.orient y) x = (p₁ : ℝ) • R₁.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₁.mult y : ℝ) • R₁.orient y) x + (p₂ : ℝ) • R₂.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₂.mult y : ℝ) • R₂.orient y) x) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = (p₁ : ℝ) * R₁.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) + (p₂ : ℝ) * R₂.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem: "The functions θ_S ξ_S(ω) and θ_T ξ_T(ω) are bounded by θ_S ‖ω‖_∞ 1_{tsupport ω}, resp. θ_T ‖ω‖_∞ 1_{tsupport ω}, a.e. on their carriers, hence integrable", followed by integrating the pointwise identity. Here it is stated for a general integer combination, as printed in Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756: p₁T₁ + p₂T₂, p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ); τ(M, θ, ξ) is Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 (‡) (lines 733–745). The selected theorem uses it with p₁ = 1 and p₂ = −1. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsdic_imrep_action_int_combination (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.integer_combination-a1.combination_action-a1, status accepted, candidate faacb9c), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. The title, statement and Lean type are copied from its DAG record, and the numbered argument below is copied verbatim from its accepted handoff; the accepted formalization follows it. Notation: μ := μHE[n]; for an IMRep R' = (M', θ', ξ') put F_{R'}(x) := 1_{M'}(x)θ'(x)ξ'(x) ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P), so the hypothesis reads F_R = p₁F_{R₁} + p₂F_{R₂} μ-a.e. Fix a test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U): ω is smooth, hence continuous, with compact support K := tsupport ω ⊆ U; put W := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞ (operator norm on n-covectors), and note ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ K.

1. Norm bound. If v is a unit orientation of some Q, i.e. v(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal τ, then |v(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ |α|·∏_i|τ_i| = |α| for every n-covector α (operator norm bound of continuous alternating maps, Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).

2. Integrability. Let R' = (M', θ', ξ') be any IMRep in U. The function h(x) := θ'(x)ξ'(x)(ω(x)) is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M' (θ' is Borel; ξ' is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M'; ω is continuous; the evaluation map (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous). By the field orients and step 1, for μ⌞M'-a.e. x, |h(x)| ≤ θ'(x)|ω(x)| ≤ W θ'(x)1_K(x). The bound is integrable on M': its integral is W∫⁻_{M'∩K} θ' dμ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult (K is compact and K ⊆ U). Hence h is integrable on M'.

3. Rewriting the action. For an IMRep R' as in step 2 and every x, F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) = 1_{M'}(x)h(x). As M' is Borel, R'.action ω = ∫_{M'} h dμ = ∫_{ℝ^P} F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x), and x ↦ F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable by step 2.

4. Conclusion. Evaluating the hypothesis at ω(x): F_R(x)(ω(x)) = p₁F_{R₁}(x)(ω(x)) + p₂F_{R₂}(x)(ω(x)) for μ-a.e. x. Integrating over ℝ^P (integrals of a.e.-equal functions agree; linearity of the Bochner integral for the integrable functions x ↦ F_{R_i}(x)(ω(x)) of step 3) and using step 3 three times:
   R.action ω = ∫ F_R(ω) dμ = p₁∫ F_{R₁}(ω) dμ + p₂∫ F_{R₂}(ω) dμ = p₁ R₁.action ω + p₂ R₂.action ω. ∎
